scope: Named Asian pear cultivars (Pyrus pyrifolia, P. bretschneideri and Asian-type hybrids such as Juicy Jewel) shippable to Annandale, NJ (zone 6b/7a). Trees grafted on callery pear (Pyrus calleryana, invasive in NJ) are left out, and so are Asian × European crosses sold as such (Maxie) and multi-variety combo trees. Most Asian pears need a second variety that blooms at the same time; known bad pairs are Nijisseiki × Kikusui, Shinsui × Kikusui, Hosui × Niitaka and Kosui × Shinsui, and Niitaka can't pollinate others.

varieties.name: Korean Giant
varieties.summary: Huge, very sweet late pear that stores for months; strong fire blight resistance.
varieties.description: A Korean pear sold as Olympic, Korean Giant or Dan Bae. Very large (up to about 1 lb) golden-brown russeted fruit, crisp and very sweet, ripening in October and keeping up to 5 months. Precocious and very resistant to fire blight; needs a pollinizer such as Hosui, Shinsui or Yoinashi.

varieties.name: Shinko
varieties.summary: Large, late, sweet russet pear; among the most fire blight resistant.
varieties.description: A Japanese pear raised before 1941. Large, round, thick brown russet, juicy and sweet, picked late and keeping 4–5 months. Upright, productive and fire blight tolerant, with abundant pollen that makes it a good pollinizer.

varieties.name: Hosui
varieties.summary: Often rated the best-flavored Asian pear; juicy, sweet-tart, late August.
varieties.description: A Japanese release from 1972 ((Kikusui × Yakumo) × Yakumo). Medium-large golden-brown russet with very juicy, fine-grained, sweet-tart flesh, ripening mid to late August and storing 3–4 months. Vigorous and spreading; susceptible to fire blight. Pollinize with Shinsui, Nijisseiki or Kosui (not Niitaka).

varieties.name: Shinseiki
varieties.summary: Yellow, mild and juicy; one of the most reliably self-fertile.
varieties.description: A Japanese pear ("New Century") from the 1940s. Medium, round, smooth yellow skin and crisp, mild, sweet white flesh, ripening in August and keeping 4–6 months. Tends toward self-fruitful and is widely used as a pollinizer.

varieties.name: Nijisseiki
varieties.summary: The classic 20th Century pear: smooth yellow, crisp and mild.
varieties.description: A chance seedling found in Chiba, Japan in 1898. Round, smooth yellow-green, crisp and mild, ripening in August to September and storing to about January. Heavy setting and needs thinning; skin can crack after rain; one of the most fire blight susceptible. Do not pair with Kikusui.

varieties.name: Chojuro
varieties.summary: Butterscotch-flavored russet pear that keeps up to 5 months.
varieties.description: A chance seedling found by Tatsujiro Toma in Japan in 1889. Medium, flattened, fully russeted fruit, firm and sweet with butterscotch notes, storing up to 5 months. Partly self-fertile and a good partner for Hosui, Nijisseiki, Kosui and Shinsui; susceptible to fire blight.

varieties.name: Kosui
varieties.summary: Small to medium, very juicy and sweet; early.
varieties.description: A Japanese release from 1959 (Kikusui × Wasekozo). Small to medium, golden-tan, very juicy, high-sugar low-acid fruit ripening mid-August; keeps about 2 months. Susceptible to fire blight. Pollinize with Hosui, Chojuro or Nijisseiki (not Shinsui).

varieties.name: Shinsui
varieties.summary: Very early, sweet and crisp; short storage.
varieties.description: A Japanese release from 1965 (Kikusui × Kimizukawase). Small to medium golden-brown russet, crisp and sweet, among the first to ripen; short shelf life. Pollinize with Nijisseiki or Chojuro; not Kosui or Kikusui.

varieties.name: Kikusui
varieties.summary: Yellow-green, sweet-tart, mid-season.
varieties.description: A Japanese pear from 1927 (Taihaku × Nijisseiki). Medium, smooth yellow-green, high in sugar and acid; skin can crack after rain; stores up to 5 months. Incompatible with Nijisseiki and Shinsui; pair with Chojuro, Hosui or Kosui.

varieties.name: Niitaka
varieties.summary: Large, late russet pear; a poor pollinizer itself.
varieties.description: A Japanese pear from 1915 (Amanogawa × Imamura Aki). Large, russeted, mild and sweet, picked late and storing up to 5 months. Its pollen is nearly sterile, so it needs a partner but can't serve as one; Hosui is incompatible. Susceptible to fire blight.

varieties.name: Atago
varieties.summary: Very large, crisp, late keeper.
varieties.description: A Japanese pear introduced in 1928, from a Nijisseiki seedling. Large to very large golden-brown russet, crisp, harvested mid-September to mid-October and an excellent keeper. Long, profuse bloom makes it a good pollinizer, but it isn't self-fertile; fire blight resistance varies by region.

varieties.name: Yoinashi
varieties.summary: Aromatic, butterscotch-flavored russet pear.
varieties.description: Introduced about 1987 by Fowler Nurseries in California. Large, round, brown russet, crisp and juicy with a butterscotch flavor, ripening between Hosui and Shinko and storing 2–3 months. Somewhat self-fertile; moderate fire blight tolerance.

varieties.name: Tsu Li
varieties.summary: Old Chinese pear-shaped variety that sweetens in storage.
varieties.description: An old Chinese heirloom. Medium-large, oval with a neck, thick yellow-green skin, crisp and juicy, improving after months in storage. Blooms early; partly self-fruitful, pairs with Ya Li or Bartlett; somewhat fire blight resistant.

varieties.name: Ya Li
varieties.summary: Classic Chinese pear-shaped variety; very early bloom.
varieties.description: An old Chinese variety (Pyrus bretschneideri). Medium-large, glossy pale yellow-green, mildly sweet and crisp, ripening late. Blooms very early, so late frosts are a risk in NJ; Tsu Li is the usual partner.

varieties.name: Daisui Li
varieties.summary: Very large green pear from UC Davis (Kikusui × Tsu Li).
varieties.description: Patented in 1988 by Ben T. Iwakiri for the University of California (Kikusui × Tsu Li). Large to very large (12–16 oz), smooth green, firm, crisp and sweet-subacid. Blooms early; not self-fertile.

varieties.name: Shin Li
varieties.summary: UC Davis cross of Chinese and Japanese pears.
varieties.description: Developed at UC Davis as a cross between Chinese and Japanese pear varieties. Limited independent detail gathered so far.

varieties.name: Juicy Jewel
varieties.summary: University of Minnesota's cold-hardy Asian-type pear (zone 4).
varieties.description: The University of Minnesota's first Asian-type pear (Shinseiki × Summercrisp), hardy to zone 4 and described as relatively free of disease, including fire blight. Crisp Asian-style fruit; needs a cross-pollinator such as Summercrisp.

varieties.name: Peggy
varieties.summary: Stark exclusive; sport of the Korean pear Arirang.
varieties.description: A mutation found on an Arirang branch in Yakima, Washington in 2003 and sold only by Stark Bro's. Needs a pollinator within 100 ft. Limited independent detail gathered so far.

varieties.name: Guam Chum
varieties.summary: Korean pear sold by Edible Landscaping.
varieties.description: A Korean pear rated for zones 6–8 by Edible Landscaping; not self-fertile. Limited independent detail gathered so far.

varieties.name: Tennosui
varieties.summary: Low-chill Japanese pear sold as self-fertile.
varieties.description: A Japanese pear sold as self-fertile with about 400 chill hours. Limited independent detail gathered so far.

varieties.name: Raja
varieties.summary: Vigorous tree with golden-brown sweet fruit.
varieties.description: A golden-brown, sweet Asian pear on a very vigorous tree. Limited independent detail gathered so far.

varieties.name: Ichiban Nashi
varieties.summary: Early, mild pear with butterscotch undertones.
varieties.description: An early Asian pear with medium-large fruit and mild butterscotch undertones; sellers report Pseudomonas resistance. Origin not documented.

varieties.name: Hamese
varieties.summary: First Asian pear of the season (mid-August).
varieties.description: Sold by Raintree as the first Asian pear of the season, ripening mid-August, sweet and crisp; needs a pollinizer. Limited independent detail gathered so far.

varieties.name: Mishirasu
varieties.summary: Huge, oval, orange-brown fruit.
varieties.description: Sold by Raintree for its huge oval orange-brown fruit. Limited independent detail gathered so far.

varieties.name: Seuri
varieties.summary: Round, bright orange medium pear.
varieties.description: Sold by Raintree for round, medium, bright orange fruit. Limited independent detail gathered so far.

varieties.name: Ooharabeni
varieties.summary: Asian pear sold by Raintree.
varieties.description: Sold by Raintree among its Asian pears. Parentage not confirmed; limited independent detail gathered so far.

varieties.name: Mount Vernon
varieties.summary: Asian pear selected at WSU Mount Vernon.
varieties.description: An Asian pear associated with Washington State University's Mount Vernon station and sold by Raintree. Limited independent detail gathered so far.

varieties.name: Reddy Robin
varieties.summary: Red-blushed Asian pear.
varieties.description: A trademarked Asian pear with red-blushed fruit, sold by Raintree and Roots to Fruits. Parentage not confirmed; limited independent detail gathered so far.

varieties.name: Shinglo
varieties.summary: Asian pear sold by Restoring Eden.
varieties.description: Sold by Restoring Eden. Limited independent detail gathered so far.

varieties.name: Pai Li
varieties.summary: An ancient Chinese pear with large, greenish-yellow fruit that stores well into winter.
varieties.description: Pai Li (also called Bai Li or Beijing White, 白梨) is an ancient Chinese pear cultivar grown in the Beijing region for centuries. It bears large, rounded, greenish-yellow fruit with sweet, juicy flesh that keeps well in storage. The tree is a vigorous grower reaching about 25 feet, hardy in USDA zones 5-9.
